explanation: I found no single Mathlib lemma stating that if `n - k` is even then `|n| - k` is even. I searched Mathlib for parity lemmas about absolute values (`even_abs`, `Even.abs`, `natAbs_even`, `odd_abs`, and any `Even` statement involving `abs`). The closest results are `odd_abs` (`Odd |a| ↔ Odd a`), `Int.natAbs_even` and `Int.natAbs_odd`. There is no `even_abs` for `|·|`, and nothing that combines absolute value with a difference. Getting the result from Mathlib would mean combining `Int.even_sub` with a parity-of-`|n|` fact (via `natAbs` or `odd_abs`, or a case split). That is more than one declaration plus routine glue.
